html:
The Movima are an Indigenous people of the Llanos de Moxos, the seasonally flooded savannas of the Beni in northeastern Bolivia. Their language has no proven relatives, and about 1,400 of them still speak it.

They lived on raised ground among the floodplains, farming and fishing. In the late 1600s and 1700s the Jesuits drew them into the Moxos missions, along with the Mojeño, the Baure and the Itonama, much like the reductions of Paraguay. After the Jesuits were expelled in 1767, ranchers and rubber traders took over the region. The town of Santa Ana del Yacuma is their centre today.
